utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that there was one preliminary about a document of which a translation should be replaced. Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. The document in question is P00468, which was admitted through Ms. Hanson on the 7th of November, 2012. The English translation contains a translation of the entire gazette from which Article 42 was taken as opposed to the one page of Article -- of Article 42, and so we're asking leave to instruct the Court Officer to remove from e-court pages 2 to 102 of the English translation, which would leave only page 1, which is the page that includes the translation of the article in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it there's no objection to the suggestion. I see there's not. Leave is granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to inform the parties that I announced yesterday that we will have a late start tomorrow at 10.30 due to technical problems with Courtroom I, that the problems have been resolved in a different way and that we therefore will start as originally scheduled at 9.30 in the morning and sit our normal hours. I also announce to the parties where we were scheduled to sit in Courtroom I next week, due to these same problems, that without the change in the schedule, we'll sit in Courtroom III next week, including a videolink. Then the -- the Chamber has decided that the Prosecution's request to -- that leave to reply would be granted to the Defence's response to the Prosecution's 92 ter motion in relation to the witness Thomas, that a request is granted, but I think we have put it already on the record that it should not become a routine and only if new matters arise the Chamber will in the future grant such requests. Having said this, any other preliminaries? If not, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I can put the following on the record: To the extent the transcript would leave any doubt as to the admission of some associated exhibits for Witness RM110, P494 was admitted into evidence or at least is now admitted into evidence, if there's any doubt, under seal and the same is true for P496.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Thomas. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas. Please be seated. Mr. Thomas, you will first be examined by Ms. Bolton, and Ms. Bolton is counsel for the Prosecution, and you'll find her to your right. Please proceed, Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Thomas. I just want to remind you before we start that you and I obviously speak the same language, and there is a court reporter who is going to be trying to keep up with us, as well as translators, so it's important that we speak a little more slowly than we would normally, and most importantly, that we try to pause between question and answer, okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter 28524, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, you should see before you a document in English. Do you recognise that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And is this a copy of the statement that you provided to the Office of the Prosecution back in May 2009?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could we go to page 43 in the English version only, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters are kindly asking that the pause between questions and answers be observed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: We've already gone off the rails.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature, sir, on page 43?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Is that your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I please have 65 ter 19695, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: This is a document, sir, entitled "Clarifications and corrections to statement." Do you recognise the signature on that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Does that document set out the clarifications and corrections that you wish to be made to your statement of 13 May 2009?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And with those clarifications and corrections, would your statement of May 2009 accurately reflect the information you wish to provide to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And if you were asked similar questions as were posed to you in 2009, if you were asked those questions today, would you give similar responses?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And having taken today the solemn declaration affirming that you would be truthful, do you affirm the truthfulness of your May 2009 statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that both the statement and the clarifications and corrections be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, no objection to the clarifications. We do have an objection to the statement, specifically paragraph 120 of the statement refers to documents that are not being tendered through this witness according to the latest list from the Prosecution and which date at a time period before and after the witness's sojourn in the Balkans and for which he don't have personal knowledge. So I submit that the descriptions of those documents and what is contained therein in paragraph 120 should be redacted or stricken from the statement if they are no longer being presented as stand alone documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I take it that my friend's requesting only redactions of the incidents where we have indicated we are not seeking to introduce those reports in relation to paragraph 120?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the ones that are outside of his time period, if there are any overlap. I think most of those are the ones that are not being tendered as associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection to redacting the documents in which respect of which it has indicated it does not intend -- or has not included on its exhibit list. However, there are four documents -- sorry, five documents, approximately, under paragraph 120 which we are seeking to have introduced through this witness, having --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please list them, making reference to -- perhaps to the hardcopy pages so that the Chamber is aware of which ones you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. Page 40 in the English version, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There is a document that's dated 24th July 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the Sitrep Increp.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That one remains, may I take it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I would like it to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The next document below that is a document from the 11th of July, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Report synthesising everything that came in from the sectors.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Correct. The document below that from the 13th of July, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the same type of document. That's how it starts. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Turning the page, Your Honours, to page 41, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Is a second document -- sorry, is the first document, I believe 11th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Starting with "This is a typical example of ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Correct. The second document on the page from the 15th, 16th, it says March 1994 but it's actually corrected to 1995 in the clarifications and corrections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Starting with "This is a simple patrol report ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And then turning the page, Your Honour, onto page 42. The third document from the bottom, from the 28th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Starting with a complete -- "this appears to be an UNMO-prepared document."

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Correct. And then the document that follows from the 30th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Starting with "This appears to be an UNMO-prepared document" as well. I can see that it reports 31 persons killed. One second. You said, sorry, five documents. If I --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in fact, it's seven, Your Honours. I said approximately five, and it's actually seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Two I do not object to, so it is actually five, but there are two from July of 1994 which are -- which are within the time period that this witness was on mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the 11th of July document and the 13th of July document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that is clear and on the record. The Chamber will decide on it once we have looked at it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a bit closer. All the others, not tendered. Ms. Bolton, you may proceed, and there -- in -- apart from this paragraph 120 still to be decided upon in relation to certain documents ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could numbers already be assigned. The Chamber, of course, is at the point to admit into evidence the statement, but we'll still consider paragraph 120. For practical purposes, I think it would be good for you to know, Ms. Bolton. And the clarification and corrections. Mr. Registrar, the first one, the report would receive number -- the statement would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 28524 becomes Exhibit P503, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P503 is marked for identification awaiting a final decision on paragraph 120. Then the clarifications and corrections to the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 19695 becomes Exhibit P504, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just looking at -- to -- in relation to paragraph 120. There is no objection against -- there's only one 15th and the 16th of March document which is still -- P504 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: With Your Honours' permission, may the witness have before him a copy of his statement to follow along with?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may be given to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And with your leave, Your Honour, may I read a summary of the witness's evidence into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Roy Thomas is a retired member of the Canadian Armed Forces. He served as the senior military observer in Sarajevo from October 1993 until the middle of July 1994. When he arrived in Sarajevo, the city was already under siege by the Bosnian Serb Army. Major Thomas gives evidence about the artillery assets of the Bosnian Serb forces. He also gives evidence to the effect that the Bosnian forces with the city were only lightly armed. Major Thomas will testify or has testified in his statement that between October 1993 and the shelling of the Markale market on the 5th of February, 1994, the BSA shelled the city of Sarajevo on a regular basis. Much of the shelling appeared random. In other words, it did not appear to be aimed at any military object. And appeared to be designed to terrorise the population. Major Thomas has authenticated daily situation reports recording some of the shelling activity. Those situation reports include grid references which have been plotted onto maps of Sarajevo. Major Thomas has examined those maps during proofing, and I will be asking him some questions about them. Major Thomas will testify that the UNMOs were not given evidence -- or has testified that UNMO's were not given freedom of movement in all areas on the Bosnian Serb side of the confrontation line, and in particular, they had difficulty accessing an area north-east of the city near Radava. And in particular, they were prevented from gaining entry to this area for approximately two weeks prior to the shelling of the marketplace. After the Markale market shelling took place, both warring factions entered into a cease-fire. Major Thomas was present during some of the negotiations over the locations of the weapon collection points and has given evidence about his observations of General Galic and will also give evidence today about his observations of General Milovanovic. Major Thomas has indicated that after the cease-fire sniping increased, and his witness statement includes a list of notorious sniping locations for Bosnian Serb snipers. And he has authenticated a number of documents relating to sniping and explained how casualties were recorded. Finally, Major Thomas was present in April 1994 at negotiations held which included General Mladic over the Bosnian Serb offensive in the safe area of Gorazde. He has evidence regarding his observations of General Mladic during those negotiations and indicates in his statement that the UNMOs were taken technically hostage following NATO air-strikes, and I anticipate he will give evidence today that UNPROFOR personnel were treated in a similar manner. That ends the summary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The translation is more or less finished, Ms. Bolton. Could you please keep your speed of speech in mind. If you have any additional questions, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Major Thomas, according to your statement, you arrived in the Sarajevo area in October 1993. Can you tell the Court what the situation was in the Mount Igman area at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. There was a confrontation because there had been an August offensive attempting to sever the connection between the Hrasnica area and the Bosnian holdings in Central Bosnia, and then there was a cease-fire arranged, or, General Mladic stopped the offensive sometime in the middle of August and Mount Igman became an area of confrontation because there was some dispute over a very tactical piece of ground which dominated the road up to what was the Olympic -- one of the Olympic ski sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You indicate that there had been an offensive in August 1993. Which forces led the offensive?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: That was an offensive undertaken by the Bosnian Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And from whom or what sources did you obtain your information about the Igman offensive?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The first source was a fellow Canadian who was the UNMO military observer operations officer in Sarajevo at the time, and the second person was my team leader who was present before I arrived on the Lima side, Major Pedersen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what was your information with respect to the role that General Mladic had played in that offensive?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: In their opinion, he was the leader of the offensive. He gave all the orders and directed everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'd like to move to a separate area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, what the opinion was of the sources is of course interesting to know. Even more interesting is to know on what they based their opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you know -- His Honour has asked do you know what the information was on which your sources relied?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. The UN military observers were requested from the very start of this offensive to get as much information as possible. Major Pedersen was responsible for the actual -- providing UNMO teams to get as close to the conflict as possible, and the Canadian operations officer that was in Sarajevo would have been responsible for monitoring the flow of information back from the military observers who would have been deployed in any safe area in Mount Igman that they could get observation on this offensive. And both of them would be tracking the location of both of the belligerent parties and their own personnel. In fact, I would suggest without -- that the military observers would know more about the situation than the -- for example, the headquarters in Sarajevo of the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even being in the field does not automatically explain why you could qualify the role of Mr. Mladic as the leader of the offensive. It's still not entirely clear to me. If you are able to further explain, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in discussion about what the tactics with these -- both these gentlemen, they told me that the exercise was designed by General Mladic and that he was there to make sure it was carried out the way he wanted it. And so they felt that this was definitely an offensive that came from him and he made sure it was carried out the way he wanted it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's a feeling, apparently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no, they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, you said, "... and that he was there to make sure ..." Did they talk about his presence during this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I want to move to an issue of respecting the time period between your arrival in October 1993 and the day of the shelling of the Markale market in February 1994. So we can focus on that time period. At paragraph 43 and 44 of your statement, you indicate that at the time of your arrival in Sarajevo, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps was surrounding the city and that their policy appeared to be one of holding. And you also indicate that you didn't witness any Serb tactical assaults. What do you mean by a tactical assault?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: What I mean by a tactical assault is where they tried to seize a tactical objective on the ground and, for example, a part of the trench line or some high ground or dominating feature. Does this satisfy the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I ask that 65 ter 10569 be brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: While that's being brought up, Major, at paragraph 83 of your amalgamated statement, you made reference to a briefing that you attended either upon your arrival in Sarajevo or immediately before arriving in Sarajevo, at which time you were provided some information, including information about heavy weapons that were in the possession of the Bosnian Serb forces. My question is looking at the document that's before you, is this a document you received during that briefing?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, and you will note that my initials are on the corner, "FRT."

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And looking at page 1, under Sarajevo-Romanija Corps there's a list of names, Sarajevo 1, Ilidza, Rajlovac, Arty-Pale, et cetera. What are those items that are listed?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: They're listing the brigades of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and some separate artillery groups; for example, artillery Pale, artillery Mokro, and the engineers, and also there's a military police element.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And so the other nine names would be the list of brigades?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And may I have, please, page 8 in English and page 9 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The document before you in English is titled "Commanders Sarajevo-Romanija Corps," and has a list of names, including General Galic, Colonel Milosevic, Colonel Indic. Are any of these individuals persons with whom you had dealings during your time in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. I dealt mainly with Major Indic and with General Galic, and Major Indic had an assistant in his liaison office which his name isn't shown there, but it's pencilled in underneath, liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In subsequent pages there are lists of additional personnel names. Could you tell me whether the information that was provided to you in this document proved to be accurate or inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: In most cases it proved to be accurate. I can't verify as I never met the brigade commander that was over the area of Radava, whether in fact it was the brigade commander who was there because I never met him. So there were several brigade commanders I didn't meet, so I can't verify all the information, but the names of personalities that I met was correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And can you just tell us which -- going by the name of the brigade, which commanders you recalled meeting?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I remember meeting and dealing with the commanders of the Ilidza brigade, the Vogosca brigade and also the Mount Igman brigade. I do -- did contact somebody in the brigade based in the area of -- between Pale and Sarajevo, but I can't remember whether in fact I met the brigade commander or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be tendered in evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 10569 becomes Exhibit P505, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May have exhibit -- or 65 ter 14963, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The document that's being brought up, sir, is a document that you discuss at paragraph 119 of your statement, and you describe it there as a list of weapons observed on the Lima side of the confrontation line. Which forces were on the Lima side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serb Army was on the Lima side.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And who prepared this list?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: This was done by military observers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And can you just assist us with some of the acronyms?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, you will see there that -- that the Lima 1 team had in its -- in its area for which it was responsible, they had found three 120-millimetre mortars, four 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you please slow down for the interpreters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry. I just want to ask you specifically what some of the short forms stand for. So could you tell me ARTY?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, A-R-T-Y, ARTY.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: ARTY stands for artillery; SP stands for self-propelled; HOW stands for howitzer; MBRL, multiple-barrel rocket-launcher; mortar is mortar; Romeo Romeo, or RR, would be recoilless weapon; and AAA is an anti-aircraft gun; and TK is the short form for tank; APC is armoured personnel carrier; the Praga is an armoured vehicle with anti-aircraft weapon system; and the APC, the BOV 1 is also an APC as its specified.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the only short form you missed was ZIS. What's that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: That's an anti-aircraft system, if I remember rightly. I can't be sure on that particular one any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could that be marked as the next exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 14963 becomes Exhibit P506, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter 10957, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The document that is being brought up, sir, is a document you discuss at paragraph 74 of your statement where you identified it as a list of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I may assist, I think it's 19057.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the correct document. Thank you to my friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: This is the document, sir, that you describe as a list of possible targets for air-strikes if the weapons weren't moved into weapons collection points following the February cease-fire agreement. I have a couple questions for you. There's -- first of all, the BSA in this document, that stands for what?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Bosnian Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And there is a reference to something called an S-P-A-A-G, SPAAG. Do you know what that's a short form for?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: At this time, no. It's -- at one time I would have known, I don't know now, can't remember. It's a weapon system.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There is a column that has a series of digits. It's preceded by the letters BP, and there are either six digit or eight digit numbers. What are those numbers?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Those are grid references, and the BP stands for the map sheet that's being used.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Have you had experience in your career of calling down artillery?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And when you call down -- sorry. Was that with which armed force or forces?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: It's with the Canadian Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And when you call down artillery with the Canadian Armed Forces, how do you identify your target?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: At the time we identified targets with grid references, normally at minimum of six figure grid references, but we would -- ideally the artillery for accuracy would like ten-figure grid references.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And within what radius can you identify a target with a six-figure grid reference?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: You can get within a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how about eight-figure --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you kindly slow down for the interpretation. It's very precise and there are a lot of figures. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, could I urge you to also listen to the interpreters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The question was, sir: Within an eight-grid reference, how close -- or how precisely can you identify a target?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Then you're starting to narrow the box. You're telling the artillery that it's within a ten-metre box. So you work from four-figure grid references, a kilometre, six-figure is a hundred metres, and the eight-figure is putting it ten metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And when you call down fire in the Canadian Forces, in addition to providing the grid reference or identifying your target, what other information would you provide?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, you have -- our procedures would have eyes on the target and after the first volley was fired there would be a damage assessment done which determines the amount of ammunition to be used in the subsequent volleys and perhaps a change in the type of ammunition. So there would always be a damage assessment made of artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You refer in your statement to something called harassing fire. In the Canadian Armed Forces, what level of command can call down harassing fire?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, the practice is normally it -- harassing fire is called down by a higher headquarters, and you may not actually have eyes on the target, but you're dropping it in an area where there may or may not be enemy traffic such as a bridge crossing or a choke point in the forest, and you're hoping to interfere with movement up to the battle-field or up to a tactical battle.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I tender this document, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 19057 becomes Exhibit P507.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Ms. Bolton, I would have one question. The third page -- the second page in e-court says page 3 of 3. The first page in e-court says page 2 of 3. Is there any cover page known or --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I believe the witness actually indicates in his statement that the first page of this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: -- is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I remember to have read that. Please proceed, and apologies for not recalling this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter 13785, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And this is, I believe, discussed at paragraph 21 of your statement. The date on this says 6 February 1994. Does that correctly represent the locations of -- I'm sorry, P2, P5, the observations posts at that date?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Actually, it -- it reflects the observation post's locations when I arrived in October.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Looking at the map, could we move the larger version of the map over a bit in English, please. You're cut off on the right side. Thank you. There appears to be a fairly large gap between L3 and L4. Could you tell me where Radava is relative to L3 and L4?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Generally almost in the middle in a north-east direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And generally, how much access were you UNMOs given to that area between L3 and L4 during your time in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: It was the most unknown area in my command.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recall whether there was any effort by any UNMO to access the area near Radava immediately preceding the Markale market shelling in February 1994?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. We had tried for several weeks in advance of that date to send patrols through that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton. Now you may proceed. Could I also ask the witness to take a short break between question and answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you indicated you had made efforts to -- or the UNMOs had made efforts to access that area. And who prevented you from accessing that area?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serb Army check-points, and we failed to get authority from the corps headquarters, or they did not influence the check-points through their brigade commander to let us in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do I take it from that answer that you tried both at the local level to gain access and also at the corps level?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, that is the brigade commander I never met, and I was never able to get access to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Was any explanation offered as to why you weren't being afforded access?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: No, not that made sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Any that didn't make sense?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: They -- they just said that we didn't need to go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I ask that this be tendered as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now translation has finished. Ms. Bolton, you really have to slow down. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 13785 becomes Exhibit P508, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I'm just trying to ascertain on which channel the B/C/S translation is so I could hear it. I've been watching the transcript to try not to go too fast, but I'd like to know what channel the B/C/S is on so I don't go too fast for the translators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I follow now and then the French booth, and they have serious problems as well. So if you want to listen to two, or both rather slow down which assists better, but B/C/S is on channel 6. French is on channel 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 19 of your statement, sir, you indicate that one of the tasks of the UNMOs on the ABiH side of the confrontation line was to monitor incoming and outgoing fire, and on the Lima side the task was to monitor outgoing fire. Based on your own observations while in Sarajevo, could you tell us in what direction the fire tended to be? Was it -- was it more coming from the Bosnian-held positions towards the BSA positions, or the reverse, more fire from the Bosnian Serbs towards the Bosnian forces?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: There was more fire from the Bosnian Serbs towards the Bosnians in the city than the reverse.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you give us any estimate as to the ratio?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: For every Bosnian round fired, there was at least three Bosnian Serb rounds fired back or fired in addition.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did that ratio ever vary?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes there would be Bosnian Serb shelling with no Bosnian rounds at all fired. And in the case of the Kosevo Hospital, which I think is a point, the -- they would fire one round from the hospital grounds, and the retaliatory rounds would probably be in the neighbourhood of 10 or 12, depending on the fire unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You've given us quite a bit of information there, sir. First of all, when you refer to "they" firing from the Kosevo Hospital, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The Bosnians fired from the Kosevo Hospital grounds. I'll say again. The Bosnians fired from the hospital grounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, I was just waiting for the interpreters. Did you ever actually see or did any of your military observers actually observe the Bosnian firing from Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: We never observed. We only heard what we thought were rounds being fired from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you make any effort to actually investigate if they were firing from those grounds?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. We tried to catch them firing from the hospital grounds. We didn't succeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. No, Ms. Bolton. French translation has now finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You speak in your statement about efforts by the Bosnians to draw retaliatory fire. Was there ever an occasion when the Bosnian Serb Army didn't respond to the provocation?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: No, not that I can remember. There was never such an occasion. They always retaliated.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And when they retaliated, could you describe the proportionality of the response.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Many more rounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In your estimate, proportionate or disproportionate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, I think the witness has given already the proportion of ten against one, and the Chamber is able to consider the proportionality of that. Please proceed. Your previous question was asked already and -- or at least the information you were seeking was given already by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 23, line 9 and following. No. I'm wrong in my reference. It was one to ten. Please proceed. Twenty-three, line 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Had you finished?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you tell me with respect to your observers, were there ever occasions when they were attempting to count artillery and the Bosnian Serb Army was using both large rounds and smaller rounds?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what effect, if any, would that have on the ability of your observers to accurately count the incoming fire onto ABH-held territory?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The observer would probably not see the impact of the smaller round if a large round arrived just ahead or just after it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, could you find in the next one or two or three minutes a suitable moment for taking a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I probably have two more questions in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did the observers that you had on the Lima side -- or, sorry, yes, the persons, individuals, who were observing outgoing fire on the Lima side have a view of all of the BSA artillery positions around Bosnia -- around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how would that affect their ability --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: -- to count -- to count the rounds?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, they might have missed outgoing rounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be a convenient place, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break. Ms. Bolton, are you, at a normal speed of speech, on track as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I couldn't hear what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was whether you, at a normal speed of speech, are on track as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: By normal speed of speech do you mean the speech -- speed at which I actually speak or if I'm waiting for the translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you take normality as referring to you only, I would say normal speed of speech for me would be the desired speed of speech.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I would be a little behind if I am waiting for the translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you may have to think about that, because as you know, this week we have a strict regime as far as timing is concerned, agreed upon by the parties, and please keep that in mind. We take a break, and we resume at 20 minutes to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Ms. Bolton, you have used almost one hour of your one and a half hours, and in view of the special scheduling arrangement and agreement this week, the Chamber expects you to stick to the time estimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Is there a -- you said almost an hour, Your Honour, and Ms. Stewart had calculated about 55 minutes. Do you have an exact time for me? That would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was 54 minutes, as far as I was informed, and I'm considering to what extent some of the time I may have taken, but I get a printout. It should be counted for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, at paragraph 47 of your statement, you refer to some local agreements that you tried to make with the commanders of various brigades. Could you tell me whether any of those agreements ever pertained to issues that would have concerned more than one brigade's zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I was never able to achieve agreements that extended beyond the authority of the local commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in terms of their actual extent of their command, did it ever involve other brigades?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I want to turn now to some of the situation reports or sitreps that were prepared.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter 18762, please. And for the assistance of the Court, these are discussed starting at paragraphs 93 to 96 of the witness's statement. Could we please in the English version go to the second page. And also in the B/C/S version, please. The pages are out of order in e-court, Your Honours. Sorry, that don't seem to me to match. Could we go back to page 1 in the B/C/S. I don't obviously speak B/C/S, Your Honour, but that doesn't seem to me to be the same page. Can we scroll up to the top?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that -- what we find at the top of this page is found in the English latter third part, civilian usage, Increp levels. That seems to be where we are. You found it, Ms. Bolton? That is under 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We start with A, and where it starts B, it's at the top of the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, this is a daily situation report covering the period of 7th to 8th January 1994, and approximately halfway down the page we see an indication that: "Approximately 50 per cent of impacts recorded were on the front line. The remainder were directed at residential areas or areas of regular civilian usage."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move up slightly the B/C/S page. No, not the English, the B/C/S. I mean, look at the top rather than -- yes. We need to be at the previous page to follow it for B/C/S speakers. The portion you read, Ms. Bolton, is not in the B/C/S available. This seems to be first page in B/C/S, but you have read it out. Let's proceed on the basis your reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you tell us, sir, who was responsible for deciding if impacts were landing in residential areas versus the front lines?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The military observer making the report would decide using his judgement whether it was close to the confrontation line or, without question, in residential areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So if something fell within some proximity to the front lines, it would be considered falling on the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Normally in most judgements it would be a case of whether the building or where it fell was -- had a -- was in range of support weapons such as machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And whose support weapons are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, the party that's being shelled. If their support weapons were back within the range of a machine-gun, for example, 500 metres, then it could be shelled 500 metres behind the confrontation line, providing the machine-gun had a clear field of fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, the part you just read for one reason or another appears on page 5 in e-court instead. So there is something fundamentally wrong with the B/C/S version of this document, jumping from number 2 to number 9 to number 14. But that portion is found on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I ask you, sir, in the first paragraph in this document there are a series of areas identified followed by four-digit numbers. What do those four-digit numbers represent?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Those four-digit numbers give you a grid square. For example, the first number would be in grid square 8963.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And that would be a grid square on a map, I take it?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And may I please ask that we go to paragraph 9 of this report, which in English I believe is the next page, and it may be page 2 in B/C/S as well. I'm just going to -- sorry. That's -- try page 3 in the English version, please. I'm looking for paragraph 9 in the next page in the B/C/S version as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph 9 --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in the B/C/S starts at page 2 in e-court, at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 9, sir, there's an indication that there were a high level of casualties from the shelling on this particular day, which is attributed to the fact -- or appears to be attributed to the fact that the BSA guns were shelling an area used extensively by civilians as a means of avoiding sniper areas. What area are they referring to?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Immediately behind Sniper Alley and where the -- it opened up there was a big intersection, and they -- people would wait behind both sides to cross the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, when you say behind --

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Behind wrecked cars, overturned trams, whatever shelter was there, makeshift shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you say behind Sniper Alley, do you mean north, south, east --

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: It would be north.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And so you talk about civilians, and you mentioned wrecked cars and overturned trams and taking shelter. You're talking about civilians taking shelter?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in paragraph 14 on this same document. So if we could go to the next page in the B/C/S version, please. Thank you. There is a commander's assessment that indicates that there may be a link between BiH attacks in Grbavica and what could be deliberate shelling of major civilian walking route. Whose assessment was that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: That was my personal assessment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the BiH attacking Grbavica, what's that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: That's a reference to night attacks into the Grbavica area by BiH forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what made you think they might be linked?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Because the BiH attacks were posing a difficulty for the Bosnian Serb forces in that we understand they had two battalions there, but at least three attacks were made at three different areas. They were very pressed to defend that area with mechanised equipment, and the most obvious means of retaliation would be attempting to get this stopped by shelling the city, although a tactical way would be to shell the built-up area immediately close to the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Were they shelling -- the area which they were shelling, was it an area that was involved in these attacks on Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I tender that document, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 18762 becomes Exhibit P509, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Could I nevertheless, Ms. Bolton, ask you to review and compare the B/C/S and the English version. I see that in English as well we jump from one number to another, but certainly there are mistakes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Certainly. May I have 65 ter 10563, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Now, this is a situation report you discuss in your statement, sir, and you clarified that the date on the first line, the 3rd of January, 1994, was actually the correct date as opposed to the date two lines down. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: That's correct. It deals with the 2nd of January to the 3rd of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And in this report, in the first paragraph we have an indication of casualties on the BiH side, 14 people killed, including three children, five males, one female, and five unknown at the time of writing, and then 22 wounded: 5 children, 14 males, and 3 females. With respect to who would be considered a civilian casualty, could you tell us who amongst those would likely have been considered a civilian casualty?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, male -- males of an age that they could be drafted would be considered possible military casualties given the context. Of -- all females and children would be considered civilians under any case, unless they were actually killed in the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And again we see a series of grid references or four-digit numbers in this situation report. With those four-digit numbers, is it possible to plot the locations the shells are falling on a map?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: It will give you the grid square where those shells fell.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- these four-digit grids, they refer to what surface? What would be the box to say so which they would refer? What would be the size?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The box would be one kilometre, and this is to allow the duty officer in Zagreb to zero in on the areas where the shelling is reported, but it doesn't make the distinction. The big box doesn't make the distinction exactly where those rounds fell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. That's exactly. So it is precise up to one kilometre --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in the extreme. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter 19703, page 11 in both -- page 11, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, you have -- sir, you have before you a map of the Sarajevo. Did you have the opportunity during proofing earlier this week to review a series of daily situation reports from 1993 and 1994 containing map grid references?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And did you compare those daily situation reports against a series of maps that had been prepared by the Office of the Prosecution for the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And were you asked whether or not the locations cited in the daily situation reports had been correctly plotted?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, with the exceptions I noted on a paper I gave to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You were given the opportunity, sir, to make comments on a sheet of paper regarding -- or make comments regarding the accuracy of the maps?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And looking at the document before you, is this one of the maps you reviewed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And this map, sir, appears to cover the time period between the 2nd of January and the 3rd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: With respect to the comments chart, may I have 65 ter 28555, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Does this document accurately set out the comments you had with respect to the maps that you -- and daily situation reports that you compared?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And with respect to the situation report we've been dealing with from the 2nd to 3rd January 1994, there is an indication that the map squares correspond with the grid references in the situation report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Document 10562, which is the next document on the comment sheet addresses only the accuracy of two of the map squares. Do you recall if the other grid references were correctly or incorrectly mapped for that situation report?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The remaining squares were correctly mapped.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this document, the comment sheet, be introduced as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection to the comment sheet. I don't know whether the underlying 65 ter numbers are being tendered as associate exhibits. If they are, subject to the comments and objection that we made in our filing that Your Honours are still considering as to the number of associated exhibits, there's no other objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, the comments, not knowing yet what they come to, there's no objections into admission. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 28555 becomes Exhibit P510, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I ask that 65 ter 10563, which is the daily sitrep we were discussing, also be marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 10563 becomes Exhibit P511, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. And now I'm just looking at the map with the squares.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. There's -- I'm wondering if you wish me to address that issue. I will indicate that the Prosecution's going to be moving for the admission of the daily situation reports that are addressed in this chart with one exception because it was not included on our exhibit list for this witness. And we would also be moving for the admission of the maps that were compared. I do need to make one clarification with respect to the maps, however, Your Honour, which is that the maps the witness looked at were from the Karadzic case, and therefore they had Karadzic exhibit numbers on them, and the confrontation lines were in different colours than we've used in this case. And so under 65 ter 19703 I have uploaded as sub A identical maps to those that the witness compared except we've removed the references to the Karadzic exhibit numbers and we've reversed the colours so they correspond with what we've been using. So it would make sense to me that we actually introduce 19703A into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have that MFI'd for the time being so that we could have a look at it. Mr. Registrar, the A map, to say so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P512, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P512 is marked for identification. Please proceed, Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to be clear, 19703A includes a series of maps, 11 maps, that correspond to the situation reports. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Them being MFI'd at this point. We will have a look at it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you. The one situation or one situation report that the Prosecution is not seeking to have tendered because we didn't include it on our exhibit list is, for the record, 65 ter 13782, and the corresponding map has already been removed from the proposed exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all on the record. Please proceed. I think you've got approximately five to six minutes left. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart's indicating a different time. She's saying I have about 15 minutes left, so could we get the official time count?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Registrar -- before the break, it was 54 minutes. We resumed slightly after, approximately 17 minutes to 4.00, but I'll have it verified. Perhaps you use your time as best as you can at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: With respect to the cease-fire agreement, sir, that you discuss at paragraphs 97 to 100 of your amalgamated statement, you refer to accompanying General Soubirou to a series of meetings with the Bosnian Serbs regarding the number and location of weapon collection points, and this would be in February 1994. Do you recall those meetings?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And do you recall whether General Galic was present at any of those?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And do you recall whether General Milovanovic had any involvement with those discussions?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I don't recall him at the meetings. I do recall him being at a weapons collection point.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And which weapons collection point?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I don't know -- remember which one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what did he appear to be doing there?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: He was there as part of the delegation from the Bosnian Serb Army, and he was unhappy with that weapons collection point. They were inspecting the proposed weapons collection point at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And as a result of your interactions, did you have any impression as to whether General Galic had the authority on his own to determine the locations of those weapon collection points?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: No. I think he was always referring the final decision to higher authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what do you base that on?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The fact that we had the Chief of Staff from the higher headquarters present doing a ground recce, and the fact that there often seemed to be a delay in the decision, although the points did not seem to be worth delaying about.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So when you talk about delaying in a decision, who was delaying in a decision?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: That would be the corps commander, General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Ultimately the parties entered into a cease-fire agreement?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And did that have any effect on the frequency of shelling of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: There was no further shelling after the cease-fire agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And as a result of that -- sorry, was that agreement entered into by General Galic or a higher authority?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: It was agreement made actually between General Rose and the two belligerent corps commanders that as of such and such a time the following day, there would be no more artillery fire, and that's the part of the agreement that both sides adhered to from the start. There was a subsidiary part of the agreement which required heavy weapons on both sides to be collected into weapons collection points.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And do you know who -- who authorised the Bosnian Serbs to enter into that part of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: That -- I do not know exactly who authorised it, but I suspect that probably it was a higher headquarters that decided that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton you asked for the exact time. You have seven minutes left at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: With respect to sniping, after the cease-fire agreement was entered into, did that have any effect on the frequency of sniping?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what was the effect?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: The effect was that the -- both sides used sniping as a means of influencing or trying to influence the behaviour of the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: My question was about the frequency.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: It -- it increased. It kept increasing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And at paragraph 66 of your statement, you describe visiting an area called Sharpstone, which was a Bosnian Serb sniping position according to your statement, and you say there: "I do not even know the rhyme or reason of why they picked individuals to be killed." Were you talking, when you referred to individuals, about soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Civilians in that case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you ever make any attempt to locate an observation post near to Sharpstone?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Were you allowed to do so?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: We were never allowed to do so, but the negotiations were well advanced until the air-strike.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And who was it you were negotiating with?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I was negotiating through Major Indic and local representatives on the ground of the brigade responsible.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter 10567, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document called "Summary of sniping." Could you tell us whether or not this was a comprehensive list of all the sniping casualties in Sarajevo during the time period covered by the document?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: This is a list of the casualties that we recorded.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you -- was UNMOs involved in all of the casualties from sniping?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: No. Some would have been seen by other UNPROFOR forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And would -- do you believe that UNPROFOR and UNMOs captured all of that sniping activity?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I can't speak for the other UNPROFOR elements. We tried to capture all the reports of sniping that we observed ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If you didn't actually observe it then?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Then we didn't report it and we did the follow-up of investigation too.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Looking at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, could you ask the witness what year this covers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The year is 1994, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Looking at page 1 of the document, under March 23rd, there is a indication "1 X BIH C W," and then a six-digit number. The reference to BiH, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: That stands for Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So what side of the confrontation line would that individual have been on?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: It would have been someone in the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to locate that grid -- or that six-digit grid reference number yesterday?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What area of the city is that near?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Now I've forgotten. I did locate it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. Finally, sir, I want to move on to the issue of April 1994 and the attack on Gorazde which you discuss in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could this be tendered as an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 10567 becomes Exhibit P513, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 09729, please. Page 3 in both English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: While that's coming up, sir, you indicate at paragraph 111 of your statement that you attended some meetings in April -- between 7th and 9th of April, 1994, at the airport, and those meetings pertained to the Bosnian Serb attack on the safe area of Gorazde. And you also indicate that General Mladic was one of the persons in attendance. Do you recall whether there were other VRS officials in attendance?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I can't really remember at this time because General Mladic was the dominant figure, and I didn't take note of the other people.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, he appeared to be the one that was speaking for everything. Or if not, he was referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You indicate at paragraph 112 of your statement that after the NATO air-strikes, 50 of your UNMOs were taken - what you call - technically hostage. Could you tell me if those UNMOs were only in the Sarajevo area or also in other areas or ...

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I can only speak for Sector Sarajevo UNMOs, but we had military observers in Zepa and Gorazde. The ones in the safe area, of course, were not taken hostage, but we had a military observer travelling between Zepa and Sarajevo, and he was taken hostage. He was -- once he was in Serb territory, he was taken hostage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, I gave you the exact time and also that the Chamber expected you to stick to the time in view of the special agreement on scheduling this week.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have perhaps one or two minutes left. Could I ask for an exception? We did have some difficulty bringing up some documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You should ask the Defence, as a matter of fact. One or two minutes is -- no objection from the Defence. They look together with me on the clock.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: This -- sir, could you tell us if other UN personnel were also taken -- treated in a similar manner?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The document you have on the screen, sir, you'll see is purported to be from Commander Mladic, and if we could have page 1, please, both English and B/C/S. In paragraph 1, sir, there is first above the numbered paragraph 1 an indication -- sorry. Could we scroll up to the top of the page, please. In the B/C/S you can see the date is the 13th 04, 94, and you can now see that in English. We have a reference to the fact that this order is being issued due to some misunderstandings about the order of the Main Staff, number 02259. And then paragraph 1 states: "UNMO and the members of the UNPROFOR are to be accommodated in appropriate premises outside of the facilities where they have been stationed to date, that is, in the military facilities which are a potential target of the NATO Air Force, as per your choice. The premises where the observers and members of the UN will be stationed have to be secured by guards and their movement must be completely limited." Did any of -- were any of your UNMOs confined in areas that might have been potential targets for air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: I -- yes, in maybe one or two cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Which areas were those?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, Lukavica headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could ask that that be marked as an exhibit, Your Honour, and that concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know that the witness has authenticated the document or added any personal knowledge to verify the contents of the same, and I note that the copy is not signed. The original is not signed. There's no signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If there's an issue as to authenticity, I'm content that it be MFI'd. As for the witness confirming, he has provided information that the treatment of some of his personnel was consistent with the order that appears before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 09729 becomes Exhibit P514, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P514 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I take it, Your Honour, that we would address the issue of the associated exhibits after cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would be the best to do, and Mr. Ivetic seems to be agreed to that as well. Then, Mr. Ivetic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, good afternoon, Mr. Thomas. I'd like to please remind you that since we both speak the same language, we have to try to ensure a pause between the question and the answer to assist those that are trying to assist us with creating a record of these proceedings, and I'd like to begin. First of all, sir, prior to your deployment to Sarajevo on October the 15th, 1993, did you have occasion to receive any instruction or training relative to the specific constitutional or political framework of the SFRY or the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When and where did this training take place?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
utterances.text: Primarily in Canada, a two-week training session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how about the military structure of the JNA, the Territorial Defence system, or the so-called Army of BiH? Did you receive any special training or instruction as to their structure?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS
